beats.lead: Two clinics, one hospital, very different odds
beats.text: In Vienna the doctors' clinic lost about 10% of mothers to childbed fever. The midwives' clinic lost under 4%.
beats.note: Those are average rates for 1841 to 1846 at the Vienna General Hospital.

beats.name: Jakob Kolletschka
beats.role: Semmelweis's colleague. He died after a student's scalpel cut him during a post mortem, and his autopsy resembled those of the women.

beats.text: Mortality was 18.3% in April 1847. After handwashing in chlorinated lime began, June was 2.2%.
beats.note: Doctors had been going from the autopsy room straight to the delivery ward without cleaning their hands.

beats.context: Roughly how far deaths in the First Clinic fell once handwashing began.

beats.text: Most contemporaries rejected the idea, and Rudolf Virchow was among them.
beats.note: He had no theory to explain it, and germ theory had not yet taken hold in Vienna.

beats.text: He died in 1865, aged 47, of a septic wound.

beats.line: The proof was there. The theory was late.
